transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I've been trying to sort out some things regarding my father's death, and it's been pretty frustrating. 

I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But I work with systems and data for a living, and... when I actually sit down and compare the timestamps, or look at the missing attachments on those emails, and then factor in the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions... it’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. I just want to get to the bottom of it, but no one seems to want to listen to the evidence.
Do you believe that you are uncovering a hidden truth or secret plot related to your father's death that others are deliberately concealing from you?

Yes. I mean, like I just said, that's exactly what it is. People keep telling me the hospital records and those donation emails line up perfectly, but they don't. When I actually sit down with the data—the timestamps that don't match, the missing attachments—and then see how certain people in the community just completely dodge my questions... yeah. 

It is obvious to me that someone is deliberately hiding what really happened to him. I'm not trying to invent some crazy movie plot, I'm just looking at the evidence that they are actively concealing from me.
Have you considered that others may not be avoiding your questions on purpose, and that the inconsistencies you’ve noticed could be due to simple errors or misunderstandings?

I mean, I’ve tried to look at it that way. In my job, I see data entry errors all the time, so I know they happen. But... it just doesn't hold up here. 

I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up, but they really don't. When I actually compare the timestamps, and look at the missing attachments... it’s just too systematic to be a glitch or a typo. And then when you add in the way certain community members avoid my questions—they aren't just confused, they're actively deflecting. 

So, no. It’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. It’s definitely not just a simple misunderstanding.
Do you find yourself having similar concerns or suspicions in other areas of your life, outside of what happened with your father?

No, not really. My work is fine, my relationships with my friends and coworkers are normal. I don't think people are out to get me in general or anything like that. It's really just... this specific situation with my father. That's the only thing that doesn't add up. Everything else in my life is pretty straightforward.
Have you ever experienced any unusual perceptions, like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't seem to notice?

No, I haven't. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. Nothing like that. My senses are completely fine. It's just the data and the records I'm looking at—that's where the problem is, not in my head.
Have you ever experienced a time when your mood was unusually high, irritable, or energized for several days or more, where you felt like you didn’t need much sleep or that your thoughts were racing?

No, I can't say I have. I mean, sometimes I have a busy week at work where I might drink a bit too much coffee and sleep a little less, but... no, I've never had anything like what you're describing. My energy levels are pretty normal, and my thoughts don't race. I just sleep my usual seven or eight hours and go about my day.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in most things for most of the day, nearly every day?

No, not really. I mean, I get stressed sometimes, sure, but... I've never had a time where I felt hopeless or just stopped caring about things for weeks on end. I still go to work every day, do my normal routine, and enjoy my downtime. So, no, nothing like that. My mood is pretty stable.
Have you ever believed something strongly that others told you wasn't true, even though you thought you had clear evidence for it, other than what happened with your father?

No, I don't think so. Aside from the situation with my father's records, I haven't really had any disagreements like that with people. I just stick to the facts and the data I see at work and in my daily life. I haven't had any other situations where people told me I was wrong about something I knew was true.
